title.rendered: Joy: The Fruit of the Spirit | Day 2

excerpt.rendered: A Roman jail cell in Philippi, past midnight. Two missionaries with their backs bleeding, their feet locked in stocks. What the other prisoners heard was singing. The kind of joy the Holy Spirit produces does not depend on circumstances.

content.rendered:
A Roman jail cell in the port city of Philippi, past midnight. Two missionaries with their backs bleeding from public beatings, their feet locked in wooden stocks. And what the other prisoners heard, unmistakably, was singing. The kind of joy the Holy Spirit produces does not depend on circumstances.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, September 25, 2026 | The Fruit of the Spirit, Day 2

Today’s Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
Galatians 5:22-23 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Sometime around AD 50, the apostle Paul and his companion Silas were dragged into the marketplace of Philippi, beaten by Roman lictors, thrown into the inner cell of the local jail, and their feet locked in wooden stocks. They had committed no crime. They had cast a spirit of divination out of a slave girl, and her owners had lost a business. That was the whole offence. By midnight, their backs were still bleeding. The stocks were cutting into their ankles. The inner cell was dark and airless. And Luke tells us in Acts 16 that the other prisoners heard them, unmistakably, “singing hymns to God.” Not surviving. Singing. That is the paradox of the second fruit of the Spirit, and it is the paradox Paul would later write to the Galatians about from personal experience.

The Greek word for joy in Galatians 5:22 is chara. It shares the same root as charis, the Greek word for grace. That linguistic connection is not accidental. In New Testament thought, joy is the natural fruit of grace received. It is not a mood the believer manufactures. It is not a personality trait some people have and others do not. It is a supernatural gladness that the Holy Spirit produces in a heart that has been rooted in the grace of God in Christ. Because it comes from grace and not from circumstances, it does not disappear when the circumstances do. Paul and Silas had grace in the jail cell. So they had joy in the jail cell.

The Passion Translation opens up the depth of what the Spirit produces: “But the fruit produced by the Holy Spirit within you is divine love in all its varied expressions: joy that overflows, peace that subdues, patience that endures, kindness in action, a life full of virtue, faith that prevails, gentleness of heart, and strength of spirit” (Galatians 5:22-23 TPT). Joy that overflows. Not joy that trickles when circumstances allow. Joy that overflows the container. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But the fruit of the (Holy) Spirit [the work which His presence within accomplishes] is love, joy (gladness)” (Galatians 5:22 AMPC). The work which His presence within accomplishes. That is exactly what joy is. Not something you manufacture. Something He produces. Your job is to stay rooted in Him. His job is to produce the fruit.

This is why James can command something as counterintuitive as “count it all joy when you fall into various trials” (James 1:2 NKJV). James is not asking believers to enjoy the trials. He is not asking believers to pretend the pain is not real. He is naming a supernatural response the Spirit makes possible. The believer, rooted in Christ, can hold sorrow and joy in the same hand. The circumstances hurt. The joy stays. Both are real, at the same time, in the same heart, because the joy is not being produced by the circumstances. The joy is being produced by the Spirit, in a heart that has received the grace of God in Christ, regardless of the circumstances.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the fruit the Spirit is producing in you. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you do not need to manufacture joy today. You do not need to fake happiness. You do not need to pretend the difficulties are not real. What you need to do is stay rooted in Christ. Feed on His Word. Return to the cross. Rest in the grace you have already received. And let the Spirit produce, in you, the joy that Paul and Silas were singing about in a Philippian jail cell at midnight. Not the fragile joy the world sells. The unshakable joy the Spirit grows. It is one of the marks of a life that belongs to Him.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that joy is a fruit of Your Spirit in my life. Not a mood I manufacture. Not a response the circumstances produce. A supernatural gladness that the Holy Spirit grows in a heart rooted in the grace of Christ. Today I refuse to let my circumstances determine my joy. My joy rises from a deeper source. Whatever the day holds, I hold sorrow and joy in the same hand, and I trust the Spirit to produce in me what only He can produce. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Joy is the fruit of the Spirit in my life today. My joy does not depend on my circumstances. It rises from the grace I have received in Christ. I walk in joy today.
